title: Constitutum Pro Damnatione Trium Capitolorum [Definitio Fidei Sancti Chalcedoniensis Concilii]
author: Vigilius

passages.original: Unde et ego anathematizantem eum Nestorium et Eutychen et impia eorum dogmata, et consentientem his quæ a sanctissimo archiepiscopo Leone scripta sunt et ab hac universali synodo, dignum esse episcopatu decerno. Antea ergo nobis inspicienda est Eunomii interlocutio, quæ planius Ibæ episcopi intellectum asserens, quid ex ea re etiam episcopus Juvenalis sensit exponit. Dicens enim ex his quæ relecta sunt Ibam innoxium compro- batum, Pholii et Eustatbii sicut et superiores Patres comprobat sine ambiguitate judicium, ut his verbis etiam negationem Ibæ episcopi et pro eodem lba attestationem Edessenorum epistolae clericorum comprehendere videatur.
passages.english: Hence I too decree that, since he anathematizes Nestorius and Eutyches and their impious doctrines, and agrees with what was written by the most holy archbishop Leo and by this universal synod, he is worthy of the episcopate. First, then, we must examine the interlocution of Eunomius, which, in stating more plainly the understanding of Bishop Ibas, also sets out what Bishop Juvenal thought on this matter. For in saying that from what had been read out Ibas had been proved innocent, he approves without ambiguity, as the earlier Fathers also did, the judgement of Photius and Eustathius, so that by these words he seems also to include the denial made by Bishop Ibas and the attestation of the letter of the clergy of Edessa on behalf of that same Ibas.
passages.notes: The first sentence is a quotation from a conciliar vote (apparently Juvenal's), the subject 'him' being Ibas. 'Pholii et Eustatbii' and 'lba' are scanning errors for Photii et Eustathii and Iba (Photius and Eustathius, the bishops who heard Ibas's case at Tyre/Berytus). 'Edessenorum epistolae clericorum' is taken as 'the letter of the clergy of Edessa'.

passages.original: Hoc quoque ausus est dicere, quia confessionem quam fecit Thomas cum palpasset manus et latus Domini post resurrectioncm, dicens, Dominus meus et Deus meus, non esse dictam a Thoma de Christo (nec enim dicit Tbeodorus Deum esse Christum) , sed ad miraculum resurrectionis stupefactum Thomam glorificasse Deum et ista dixisse. Et quod pejus est, etiam in interpretatione quam in AcUbus apostolorum scripsit idem Theodorus, similem fecit Christum Platoni et Manichæo et Epicuro et Marcioni, dicens quod sicut illorum unusquisqoe ex dogmate quod invenit suos discipulos fecit vocari Platouicos et Manichæos et Epicureos et Marcioni stas, simili modo et cum Christus dogma invenisset, ex ipso Christianos vocari.
passages.english: He also dared to say this: that the confession which Thomas made when he had touched the hands and side of the Lord after the resurrection, saying, "My Lord and my God," was not said by Thomas about Christ (for Theodore does not say that Christ is God), but that Thomas, astonished at the miracle of the resurrection, glorified God and said these things. And what is worse, also in the commentary which the same Theodore wrote on the Acts of the Apostles, he made Christ similar to Plato and Mani and Epicurus and Marcion, saying that just as each of them, from the doctrine which he devised, caused his disciples to be called Platonists and Manichaeans and Epicureans and Marcionites, in the same way also, when Christ had devised a doctrine, [his followers] were called Christians after him.
